reason: The methane stream belongs at the methane liquefier, which seems like a direct way to address the goal of storing it dry and cold.
expectation: I expect the plant to remove water and liquefy the methane for storage, though I don't know whether that will complete the goal in one step.

alternatives.reason: Liquefying the oxygen also directly serves a goal; I chose to handle the wet methane stream first.

effect: The plant removes residual water before liquefying the methane, completing its storage goal; oxygen storage remains.
reaction: The separation of drying and liquefaction is a useful detail, and the months-long production makes the return feel distant.
reason: The oxygen liquefier is the only remaining gameplay option and directly addresses the oxygen storage goal.
expectation: I expect the oxygen to be liquefied and stored separately, though I don't know whether that completes the chapter.

effect: The oxygen now has its own cold store, completing the chapter and establishing both ingredients for the eventual departure.
reaction: The separate stores make the fuel preparations feel concrete, although they are only the beginning of a months-long wait.

mostWorthwhile.text: Liquefying the wet methane was the most worthwhile action because the result explained that residual water is removed before storage and connected production to the longer wait for departure.

leastWorthwhile.text: Storing the oxygen was straightforward and offered little decision-making because it was the only remaining gameplay option.

surprise.text: The methane store began collecting immediately, but producing the rest would take months of power and water.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary: each matched a named supply to its corresponding liquefier and storage goal.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the long production period and the effort to bring the specimens home unfold, though this chapter's choices were very direct.
